declaration.goal: Crawl ahead by 0.3 to 0.5 m, keeping within 0.2 m of the start line and within 20 degrees of the start heading.
declaration.measured_by: Computed from the simulator's pose, as the quantities a camera straight above could measure; not measured from a camera image. The camera sees a floor area of 2.59 m by 1.46 m. x, y and heading are relative to the start of each trial: x in the direction the body faces at the start, y to its left, heading counter-clockwise seen from above, in (-180, 180]. At the start the body is at x = 0, y = 0, and the view spans x from -0.84 to 1.74 m and y from -0.73 to 0.73 m. A value is lost when the camera could not see the tracked point.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c1 is held at -0.5 and c3 is a unit sine at 1.5 or 2 Hz, THE system SHALL end at x between 0.3 and 0.5 m with heading within 20 deg of zero.

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Half-strength c1 with a c3 sine gives a straight crawl of 0.3 to 0.5 m

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Half-strength c1 with a c3 sine gives a straight crawl of 0.3 to 0.5 m

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: c1=-0.5 with unit c3 sine at 2 Hz gave x -0.055, heading -7.7; at 1.5 Hz x -0.023, heading -1.2. The body hardly moved (picture strip shows almost no travel). Predicted x 0.3-0.5 missed low in both. Heading prediction hit but only because there was no motion. a1=-0.5 does not stroke forward at f 1.5-2, unlike the given f=1 result 0.263.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c1 = -1 and c3 is a unit sine at 2 Hz, and both are switched to 0 after T seconds, THE system SHALL end at x between 0.3 and 0.5 m with heading within 20 deg of zero for T = 3 and T = 3.5.

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Cutting the a1=-1, f=2 drive early stops the crawl inside 0.3 to 0.5 m

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Cutting the a1=-1, f=2 drive early stops the crawl inside 0.3 to 0.5 m

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: c1=-1 plus a unit 2 Hz c3 sine cut at T=3 or 3.5 s gave x -0.034 and -0.038, heading -5.2 both. No forward travel at all; the picture strip shows the body in place. Trajectory is nearly identical to E1 (a1=-0.5), so c1 has no visible effect here. The given rules R9, R11, R13 do not describe this system.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c0..c4 are unit sines at f = 1.5 Hz with phase lag ph = 1 per channel index, THE system SHALL end at x between 0.1 and 0.35 m; and WHEN c1 is held at +1 with the rest 0, THE system SHALL end with |x| below 0.1 m.

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: A travelling wave across all channels moves the body forward, and a constant c1 = 1 does not

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: A travelling wave across all channels moves the body forward, and a constant c1 = 1 does not

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: c1=+1 held alone gave x 2.5e-5, heading 0: no effect, as predicted. The wave at f=1.5, ph=1 gave x -0.080, y 0.076, heading -146 (it spun about +215 deg over 5 s), so P1 (x 0.1-0.35) missed. The wave at f=3 gave x -0.050, heading +113. The wave rotates the body and does not translate it.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN all five inputs are unit sines at 1.5 Hz with phase lag ph per channel index, THE system SHALL end with heading within 30 deg for ph = 0, and x between 0.3 and 0.5 m for ph = 2.

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Wave phase lag sets whether the body travels or spins

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Wave phase lag sets whether the body travels or spins

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: ph=0 gave x -0.088, heading -153 (spin, not within 30 deg). ph=2 gave x -0.018, heading +61. ph=-1 gave x -0.038, heading +55. No phase lag gives forward travel; x stays between -0.09 and 0 and the body spins or drifts in heading. Both predictions missed.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN two adjacent channels get unit sines at 2 Hz with a quarter-cycle lag and the other three inputs are 0, THE system SHALL end at x between 0.1 and 0.5 m, for the pair (c2, c3) and for the pair (c3, c4).

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: A quadrature stroke on two adjacent channels gives forward travel

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: A quadrature stroke on two adjacent channels gives forward travel

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: Pair (c2,c3) in quadrature at 2 Hz: x -0.029, y 0.160, heading +165 (spin). Pair (c3,c4): x 0.070, y 0.096, heading +0.3, steady drift in x and y of about 0.014 m/s. Both predictions missed low (x 0.1-0.5). The c3,c4 pair is the only trial with straight heading and positive x, but x is far below the 0.3 m target.
